successCriteria.description: RequestLeavePage renders a form with a leave-type select whose options are the LeaveTypeCode enum values, plus start-date and end-date inputs producing ISO date strings, and no comment/reason input.

On submit, the page calls validateLeaveRequestInput with the collected input; when it returns a non-empty error array, the errors are rendered inline and leaveService.create is never invoked (no network call).
When validation passes, the page calls leaveService.create with exactly { leaveTypeCode, startDate, endDate } and, on success, navigates to /leaves/${created.id}.
When leaveService.create rejects with an ApiError, the page surfaces the API's own error message (err.message) in a role="alert" element rather than a generic failure string.

The vitest suite in RequestLeavePage.test.tsx covers: a validation failure renders the error and never calls leaveService.create; a successful create navigates to /leaves/${id}; a rejected create surfaces the API's message.

constraints: Do not modify App.tsx or presentation/index.ts; route registration for /leaves/new is deferred to Phase 5.

The page must not mirror backend policy (min-notice, max-duration) — client-side validation is limited to the three rules in validateLeaveRequestInput; backend rejections surface via the API's own error message.
No comment/reason input is rendered; the form captures only leave type, start date, and end date.
outOfScope: Route registration of /leaves/new in App.tsx and re-export of RequestLeavePage in presentation/index.ts (Phase 5).
Any backend change; this phase is web-only and consumes the existing POST /leaves endpoint via ILeaveService.create.

entityInvariants.invariant: Submitted input carries leaveTypeCode as a LeaveTypeCode enum value and startDate/endDate as ISO date strings (never Date objects); the page never adds fields beyond these three.
The created request returned by leaveService.create is treated as opaque; the page reads only created.id for navigation and never mutates or re-derives requestedDays/status.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects with ApiError carrying the backend's own message (e.g. insufficient balance); the page must surface err.message verbatim, not a generic failure.
Returns a (possibly empty) array of human-readable error strings; a non-empty result must short-circuit the network call.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Import ILeaveService from the leave module barrel (../../modules/leave/index) and call leaveService.create with a CreateLeaveRequestInput; do not re-declare the service interface or input type.
Reuse validateLeaveRequestInput exactly as exported (three rules only); do not add min-notice/max-duration checks.
Reuse LeaveTypeCode and CreateLeaveRequestInput from shared types; the select options must be the LeaveTypeCode enum values.

Match the established form/error conventions: useState + FormEvent<HTMLFormElement> + e.preventDefault(), a submitting boolean disabling the submit button, and errors rendered in a role="alert" element with the err instanceof Error ? err.message : fallback pattern.

Match the established test conventions: vitest + @testing-library/react render/screen/fireEvent/waitFor, MemoryRouter with Routes/Route and a data-testid target for navigation assertions, and vi.fn() mocks with satisfies for typed fixtures.

integrationPoints.why: The page's only write path; delegates to the API client's POST /leaves and returns the created LeaveRequestView whose id drives navigation.
Pre-send client-side validation gate; a non-empty result prevents the network call.
Source of the select options and the submitted input shape.
